title: Sales Enablement Playbook — Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pricing, Case Studies, Security FAQ
author: Ava Martinez
body:
Overview

Summary: This playbook centralizes Redwood Inference's go-to-market messaging for prospects evaluating LLM inference platforms. It covers recommended positioning and one-liners, competitive brief talking points, pitch deck structure and slide guidance, baseline pricing guidance and negotiation levers, representative case studies, and a prospect-facing Security & Compliance FAQ. Use this as the canonical reference for AE/SDR/SE teams when preparing demos, pricing conversations, and RFP responses.

Audience: Account executives, solutions engineers, sales leadership, partner sellers.

Owner: Go-to-market (AE leadership) — update cadence: quarterly and after major product launches.

Positioning & Messaging (elevator + value props)

Elevator (30s): "Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that delivers predictable, low-latency LLM serving across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments — helping engineering teams lower per-token costs, meet latency SLOs, and maintain control over data and compliance as usage scales."

Primary value pillars (talking points)
- Performance & predictability: single-digit 99th-percentile latencies for common gen workloads (e.g., 90–512 token responses) with autoscaling and reserved pools.
- Cost efficiency: workload-aware batching, KV/prefix caching and quantization guidance that reduce per-token costs by up to 3x vs naive host-based endpoints.
- Deployment flexibility: hosted API for quick start, Redwood Dedicated for committed GPU capacity, Redwood Private for VPC/on-prem regulated workloads.
- Observability & operations: Redwood Console provides token-level cost breakdown, per-route dashboards, and rollout controls (canary/A-B/fallback).
- Risk reduction: deterministic fallbacks, version pinning, and eval-driven quality guardrails to prevent regressions.

Positioning by buyer type
- AI-native startups: emphasize rapid time-to-prototype + transparent cost controls and free trial credits.
- Platform teams: emphasize standardization, rollout controls, and rate-limiting/quota primitives.
- Enterprises/regulated: emphasize Redwood Private, KMS/HSM integration, audit logs, and compliance support.

Competitive Briefs (how to frame common competitors)

1) General cloud AI endpoints (Hyperscaler-managed endpoints)
- Strengths: integrated cloud billing, end-to-end infra.
- Redwood differentiation: Superior inference economics via optimizer (batching, caching, quantization), predictable reserved capacity, and consistent developer experience across private deployments.
- Talking points: "If your customer cares about sustained throughput and predictable latency/cost, Redwood avoids noisy neighbor and variable per-token bills by offering reserved pools and workload-aware batching optimizations."

2) LLM API providers (convenience-focused competitors)
- Strengths: large model catalogs, turnkey UX.
- Redwood differentiation: Production-grade controls (rollouts, tracing, token-level cost), private deployment options for compliance, and developer-focused SDKs with performance profiles.

3) Self-hosted inference runtimes / orchestration vendors
- Strengths: full control, potential cost savings at scale.
- Redwood differentiation: We combine an optimized serving runtime plus orchestration and product features (monitoring, billing, SLA) — reducing total cost of ownership and engineering time to production.

Pitch Deck Guidance (recommended slide flow and messaging)

Recommended slide order (10–12 slides for a discovery/demo deck)
1. Title + one-liner (30s elevator)
2. Customer challenge (latency/cost/unpredictability/compliance)
3. Redwood solution overview (hosted, dedicated, private)
4. Architecture snapshot (runtime, smart routing, caching) — include simple diagram
5. Performance & cost benchmarks (concise table, sample workloads)
6. Security & compliance (KMS/HSM, VPC, audit logs)
7. Operational controls (rollouts, console dashboards, alerts)
8. Case study (1 customer, 3 metrics improved)
9. Pricing models & TCO examples (hosted vs dedicated vs private)
10. Next steps & CTA (trial, POC, technical deep dive)

Slide tips for SEs
- Keep slides visual and metrics-driven. Use real latency/cost numbers.
- Use the Appendix for backup charts (per-token cost breakdown, benchmark methodology).
- Always include a clear CTA (e.g., "Start a 30-day POC with Dedicated capacity — contact AE for reserved pool quote").

Baseline Pricing Guidance (enablement for initial conversations)

Pricing models (canonical quick guidance)
- Redwood Hosted API: usage-based pricing with per-token generative unit and per-embedding unit. Typical public benchmark: $0.003 / 1k prompt tokens and $0.006 / 1k generation tokens for standard curated models (example only — refer to Pricing page for official rates).
- Redwood Dedicated: monthly committed capacity (GPU-hours or slot-based commitments) + discounted per-token execution for burst beyond commit. Typical enterprise commit tiers: Starter (4 x A100-equivalent slots), Growth (16 x), Scale (64 x).
- Redwood Private: platform license + deployment services + optional managed operations.

Negotiation levers for AE/SDR/SE
- Term length: 12 vs 24 vs 36 month commitments reduce unit cost.
- Commit size: larger reserved pools unlock deeper discounts and priority capacity.
- Feature bundling: premium observability retention, higher SLA, extended support windows.
- Proof-of-value: offer pilot credits or pilot discount on Dedicated pool for first 90 days.

TCO example (talking script)
"For a product generating 200M tokens/month with 50ms avg generation latency, customers who moved from pay-as-you-go cloud endpoints to Redwood Dedicated typically see a 25–45% reduction in monthly inference spend after amortizing reserved capacity and enabling batching and cache optimizations."

Case Studies (two concise examples to cite in decks)

Case Study A — Fintech analytics startup
- Pain: Real-time customer-facing summarization with strict P95 latency < 200ms.
- Redwood solution: Dedicated GPU pool with autoscaling, KV caching for prefix workloads, quantized model variant in production.
- Results: P95 reduced from 480ms to 140ms; inference cost per active user reduced by 36%; went from 1 engineer maintaining infra to 0.

Case Study B — Healthcare SaaS (regulated)
- Pain: Data residency and compliance plus auditability for model predictions.
- Redwood solution: Redwood Private deployed in customer VPC, KMS integration for keys, full audit logs surfaced in Console.
- Results: Achieved SOC2 & regional data residency requirements; onboarding time reduced by 60% vs building in-house; SLA-backed uptime enabled clinical SLA contract.

Security & Compliance FAQ (for prospects)

Q: How does Redwood handle customer data in hosted mode?
A: By default, hosted API processes requests in isolated compute; customer data is encrypted-in-transit (TLS 1.2+) and at-rest. We provide contractual controls for data use and do not persist customer inputs longer than required for operational needs; retention policies are configurable per account. For regulated workloads we recommend Redwood Private or Dedicated with strict retention settings.

Q: Can customers bring their own keys?
A: Yes. We support KMS/HSM integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, and customer HSM via private deployment). Keys for private deployments can be customer-managed.

Q: What certifications and audits does Redwood maintain?
A: Redwood maintains SOC2 Type II (2025), ISO 27001 alignment work (in_progress), and provides audit artifacts under NDA for enterprise customers.

Q: Is the platform multitenant? How do you prevent noisy neighbor effects?
A: Hosted API is multitenant but isolated by namespaces and request quotas; performance-sensitive customers are advised to use Redwood Dedicated to guarantee capacity and latency SLOs. We use autoscaling, reservation pools, and smart routing to mitigate interference.

Q: What logging/audit options are available?
A: Audit logs include request IDs, route, model version, timestamp, and user/account metadata. Logs can be exported to customer S3, SIEM integrations, or viewed in Redwood Console with retention tiers.

Example security snippet (how to request a private deployment evaluation)
1. AE/SE: Complete the Private Deployment Intake form (link in Appendix).
2. Security Review: Provide SOC2 summary, network diagram, and required compliance evidence.
3. Deployment: Onboarding runs 4–8 weeks depending on network complexity.

Appendix & Artifacts

Ownership & Next steps
- Quarterly review: GTM leadership to refresh use cases and pricing guidance post-major releases.
- AE/SE training: Recommend 60–90 minute enablement every quarter; record session and publish to docs-site.
- Feedback loop: Send gaps or competitive intel to go-to-market-intel@redwood.ai.
